question: The flat rise costs about 1.9 million pounds of the 2.4 million a year. What should the other 500,000 a year do?
options: Keep it as a reserve for checks and emergencies
Pay for training on paid time and offer voluntary guaranteed hours
Give it back to the council's general budget

jurors.profile: 68, retired, London, owns with mortgage, did not vote 2024
jurors.why: Keep it in a pot the council can call on. Money given away never comes back when you need it.

jurors.profile: 56, long-term sick or disabled, East of England, owns with mortgage, did not vote 2024
jurors.why: A reserve means the checks get paid for and a bad winter doesn't wipe out the scheme.

jurors.profile: 42, long-term sick or disabled, North West, social rent, Reform UK 2024
jurors.why: Council money sat in a fund is just money not being used. Hand it back and let the budget decide what it's for.

jurors.profile: 23, student, Northern Ireland, owns outright, Reform UK 2024
jurors.why: If it isn't needed for the pay rise, give it back. A ring-fenced pot is how money gets stuck.

jurors.profile: 64, looks after home and family, Scotland, owns with mortgage, did not vote 2024
jurors.why: I've had carers in my house. Train them properly and let them have a day off paid, and they'll stay.
Training on paid time is what keeps people in the job. A pay rise on its own doesn't teach anyone anything.

jurors.profile: 19, employed, East Midlands, private rent, did not vote 2024
jurors.why: Paid training and a proper set of hours would make me stay somewhere. Nobody offers me that now.

jurors.profile: 56, student, South East, social rent, did not vote 2024
jurors.why: Give the carers qualifications and a regular rota. Otherwise it's just a rise for a few months.

jurors.profile: 65, retired, West Midlands, owns outright, Conservative 2024
jurors.why: The council should live within its budget. Money set aside for one job goes back to the pot when the job is done.

jurors.profile: 66, retired, West Midlands, owns outright, did not vote 2024
jurors.why: Keep a reserve. Councils always find the reserve gone the year you need it.
The firms have a habit of promising things and not paying. Keep the reserve so the checks can be enforced.

jurors.profile: 39, employed, Scotland, owns outright, Liberal Democrat 2024
jurors.why: Training and guaranteed hours are what stop carers leaving. That's the point of the whole scheme.
